step1_figure.circuit_type: Fully-differential folded-cascode op-amp with output buffer and continuous-time common-mode feedback (CMFB)
step1_figure.description: Figure 26.43 shows the complete op-amp schematic providing common-mode feedback (CMFB) through just the output buffer using triode-operating NMOS transistors and an error amplifier to regulate the output common-mode level to VCM.

differential_dc_gain.description: Low-frequency differential open-loop voltage gain (Av = d(vop - vom) / d(vip - vim))

equation.explanation: Differential voltage gain determined by input transconductance gm1 and total output impedance of the two-stage amplifier with output buffer.
equation.assumptions: Output buffer operating in linear/saturation region with loaded 20k feedback averaging resistors.

sky130_expected.calculation: With input pair gm ≈ 2 * sqrt(0.5 * 270u * 10/1 * 10uA) ≈ 164 uA/V, output buffer gm2 ≈ 400 uA/V, and loaded output resistance dominated by 20k feedback network and cascodes (~1 MΩ interstage, ~20k buffer load), Av ≈ 300 - 400 V/V (≈ 50 dB to 52 dB), matching Fig 26.44(b) peak gain of ~380 V/V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Figure 26.44(b) explicitly displays op-amp differential gain peaking near 380 V/V (51.6 dB) around common-mode equilibrium.

unity_gain_frequency.description: Unity-gain (gain-bandwidth product) frequency of the op-amp

equation.explanation: Equation explicitly given on page 892 defining the op-amp unity-gain frequency with Miller compensation capacitor Cc = 25 fF.
equation.assumptions: First stage dominant pole compensation with Cc = 25 fF (C1, C2 in netlist).

sky130_expected.calculation: f_un = gm / (2 * pi * Cc) = 164 uA/V / (2 * pi * 25 fF) ≈ 1.04 GHz (loaded GBW ≈ 150 MHz - 300 MHz due to CL = 250 fF and buffer loading).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Derived directly from gm/(2*pi*Cc) using input diff-pair transconductance and Cc = 25 fF.

output_common_mode_voltage.description: Quiescent output common-mode DC level set by the CMFB network

equation.explanation: The continuous-time common-mode feedback forces the average of the differential outputs to equal VCM.
equation.assumptions: High loop gain in the output buffer CMFB error amplifier.

sky130_expected.calculation: VCM reference is set to 0.50 V (500 mV) in the netlist. The CMFB loop drives (vop + vom) / 2 to VCM = 500 mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Direct application of Eq. (26.8) with VCM = 500 mV.

differential_output_offset_gain.description: Differential output voltage shift due to input-referred offset voltage

equation.explanation: Closed-loop differential offset relationship derived from KCL at the inverting and non-inverting virtual ground nodes.
equation.assumptions: Rf = Rin = 20k resistor feedback topology as shown in Fig. 26.46.

sky130_expected.calculation: With Rf = Rin = 20k, (Rf/Rin + 1) = 2. For an input offset V_OS = 50 mV, differential output vop - vom = 50 mV * 2 = 100 mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Direct substitution of Rf = 20k, Rin = 20k into Eq. (26.13).

settling_time.description: 1% settling time for large-signal step response

equation.explanation: Settling time for transient steps defined as time to settle within the steady-state final value band.
equation.assumptions: Load capacitance CL = 250 fF and Cc = 25 fF.

sky130_expected.calculation: Page 892 states: 'The settling times are approximately 1-2 ns.'
sky130_expected.reasoning: Quoted directly from the experimental text on page 892 for this topology.

total_quiescent_current.description: Total quiescent current drawn from VDD supply

equation.explanation: Sum of currents through diff-amp stage, output buffers, CMFB amplifier, and wide-swing reference bias generator.

sky130_expected.calculation: Page 892 explicitly specifies: 'The current drawn from VDD (including the bias circuit current) is approximately 250 uA (200 uA for the op-amp alone).'
sky130_expected.reasoning: Specified directly on page 892 of the text.

step3_testbench.description: Comprehensive ngspice testbench measuring DC open-loop gain, CMFB output level, total current consumption, AC bandwidth/gain, and transient step response for Figure 26.43.
